subject: paediatrics
title: Parvovirus B19, Hand-Foot-Mouth, Scarlet Fever and Mumps

steps.tx: Erythroid progenitor cell tropism dictates the clinical spectrum of fifth disease in children. The single-stranded DNA virus **parvovirus B19 infection** binds to the erythrocyte P antigen (globoside), replicating inside nucleated erythroid progenitor cells and temporarily arresting red blood cell production. In healthy children, this manifests as erythema infectiosum, whereas patients with chronic haemolytic anaemias suffer catastrophic acute erythroblastopenic crises.
steps.say: Parvovirus B19 targets the red cell P antigen, arresting erythropoiesis. In healthy children it causes fifth disease, but in sickle cell or spherocytosis it triggers aplastic crisis.

vis.alt: Clinical spectrum of Parvovirus B19 from slapped-cheek rash to transient aplastic crisis.
vis.caption: Parvovirus B19 clinical manifestations showing slapped cheek erythema, reticular lacy rash, and aplastic crisis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The cutaneous eruption of erythema infectiosum evolves through three distinct morphologic stages. Stage one features intense confluent fiery erythema over both cheeks with sparing of the nasal bridge and perioral region, producing the classic **slapped cheek appearance**. Within one to four days, stage two emerges as an erythematous maculopapular rash over the extensor extremities that clears centrally, creating a characteristic lacy reticular network.
steps.say: Erythema infectiosum begins with a bright red slapped-cheek facial rash, followed by an erythematous lacy reticular rash on the arms and legs that waxes and wanes with sunlight.

left.title: Stage 1: Slapped-Cheek Facial Rash
points: Fiery red erythema across bilateral cheeks
Circumoral pallor sparing nasal bridge
Fades spontaneously over 2 to 4 days
Child is no longer contagious once rash erupts

right.title: Stage 2 & 3: Reticular Lacy Body Rash
points: Maculopapular rash on extensor limbs and trunk
Central clearing produces reticular lace pattern
Waxes and wanes for weeks with heat and sun
Mild symmetrical polyarthropathy in adolescents

steps.tx: Temporary cessation of marrow erythropoiesis triggers life-threatening drop in circulating haemoglobin. In children with sickle cell anaemia, hereditary spherocytosis, or thalassaemia, parvovirus B19 causes acute **transient aplastic crisis**, characterized by profound pallor, fatigue, high-output congestive cardiac failure, and complete absence of circulating reticulocytes (reticulocyte count under 0.1%). Urgent management requires packed red blood cell transfusions until marrow erythropoiesis resumes.
steps.say: In sickle cell and spherocytosis, parvovirus causes transient aplastic crisis with profound anaemia and absent reticulocytes. Urgent packed red cell transfusions are life-saving.

steps.tx: Enteroviral infection produces distinct vesicular eruptions across oral mucosa and extremities. The common condition **hand foot mouth disease** is caused primarily by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus A71, transmitted via feco-oral and respiratory routes. Children present with low-grade fever, painful oral ulcerations on the tongue and buccal mucosa, and tender oval grey vesicles on an erythematous base distributed over palms, soles, fingers, buttocks, and knees.
steps.say: Hand, foot, and mouth disease causes painful oral ulcers and oval vesicles on palms, soles, and buttocks. Enterovirus 71 strains can cause severe brainstem encephalitis.

left.title: Coxsackievirus A16 Phenotype
points: Mild self-limiting fever for 3 to 5 days
Painful shallow aphthous oral mucosal ulcers
Vesicular lesions on palms, soles, buttocks
Complete spontaneous recovery within 7 days

right.title: Enterovirus A71 Neurological Risk
points: Potential for severe systemic complications
Acute brainstem encephalitis and flaccid paresis
Fulminant neurogenic pulmonary oedema
Requires close in-hospital neurological monitoring

steps.tx: Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins trigger capillary dilatation and widespread cutaneous erythroderma. Developing secondary to pharyngeal infection with Group A Streptococcus pyogenes, **scarlet fever erythrogenic toxin** produces a fine punctate erythematous rash described as a boiled lobster blush with a rough sandpaper texture. The rash spares the face except for circumoral pallor, and petechial linear streaks called Pastia lines form along the antecubital and axillary flexures.
steps.say: Scarlet fever stems from streptococcal pyrogenic toxins. Patients present with a rough sandpaper rash, circumoral pallor, Pastia lines in flexures, and a strawberry tongue.

rows: Swollen red papillae project through fur

steps.tx: Sequential desquamation of lingual papillae generates a pathognomonic oral mucosal appearance. On days one and two of scarlet fever, the **strawberry tongue evolution** begins as a white strawberry tongue, where swollen hyperaemic red fungiform papillae project through a thick white coat. By day four, the white coating desquamates completely, leaving a beefy red, glistening red strawberry tongue. Oral penicillin V for ten days eradicates carriage and prevents acute rheumatic fever.
steps.say: The tongue evolves from a white strawberry appearance on day one to a raw red strawberry tongue by day four. Penicillin V for ten days prevents acute rheumatic fever.

left.title: Scarlet Fever Features
points: Sandpaper rough diffuse erythematous rash
Pastia flexural petechial lines
Circumoral pallor and strawberry tongue
Ten days oral penicillin V therapy

right.title: Kawasaki Disease Contrast
points: Strawberry tongue and lip fissuring present
High fever persisting >=5 days refractory to abx
Bilateral non-purulent conjunctival injection
Coronary artery aneurysms; IVIG treatment

steps.tx: Paramyxoviral infection of glandular epithelium causes painful tender salivary swelling. The rubulavirus infection **mumps parotitis** is characterized by painful swelling of the parotid glands, beginning unilaterally before becoming bilateral, lifting the earlobe upward and outward and obscuring the mandibular angle. The orifice of Stensen's duct opposite the upper second molar appears red and swollen, with serum amylase elevated secondary to salivary glandular inflammation.
steps.say: Mumps causes painful parotid swelling that elevates the earlobe and obscures the mandibular angle. Stensen duct is inflamed, and serum amylase is elevated.

steps.tx: Post-pubertal males face acute gonadal inflammatory complications following parotid involvement. Developing in up to thirty percent of post-pubertal adolescent males with mumps, **mumps orchitis** typically manifests four to seven days after parotitis onset with high fever, chills, nausea, and excruciating unilateral testicular pain and swelling. While pressure atrophy of seminiferous tubules occurs in roughly one-third of affected testes, bilateral complete testicular atrophy causing sterility is exceptionally rare.
steps.say: Mumps orchitis strikes post-pubertal males with acute testicular pain and swelling. While testicular atrophy can occur in one-third, complete bilateral sterility is exceptionally rare.

left.title: Mumps Orchitis Management
points: Bed rest, scrotal support with athletic jockstrap
Cold ice packs applied locally to scrotum
Analgesia with paracetamol and NSAIDs
Reassurance regarding low risk of sterility

right.title: MMR Preventive Immunization
points: Live attenuated mumps Jeryl Lynn strain
Two-dose schedule at 9-12 months and 4-6 years
95% long-term protective efficacy
Eliminates orchitis and sensorineural deafness
